p0.what: Neighbouring second molar hangs into the open socket as a free, tapered white fang with no interdental septum or bone around it (visible f540-f627, both root deliveries). It reads as a canine-like root exposed to its tip, which is physically wrong anatomy for the adjacent tooth. Repair: restore the septum/distal alveolar bone so only the distal crown surface of the second molar shows above the socket wall. Proof: f567 and f600 show a broad molar crown seated in bone, no pointed free end.

p1.what: Suture payoff does not close the wound: the socket opening is the same size at f690 and f720, and the knot sits beside a gaping dark hole. Repair: animate the throw drawing both flap edges together so the gap narrows to a line by the end of the shot. Proof: f725 shows approximated edges under the knot.

Bur is parked during bone removal: its tip moves about 10 px over f186-f264 while the cortex disappears in a wider pink film beside it, so the 3.5 s drill beat (longest shot) has no travelling cut. Repair: sweep the bur along the bone edge in step with the removal bands, with dust and coolant at the contact. Proof: f250 against f200 shows the tip displaced with a kerf behind it.

Needle holder vanishes and a finished knot with long tails appears between two consecutive motion-strip cells (about f709 to f713) with no tying action; reads as an in-shot pop. Repair: keep the holder on screen through the knot or cut to a new angle. Proof: f705-f715 run shows continuous holder motion or a clean angle change.

Root-division beat lasts 26 frames and the bur works underneath the root from the lower left with no visible kerf; the next shot simply shows two pieces. Repair: frame the bur crossing the root from above and leave a visible slot, hold at least 40 frames. Proof: f484 shows a slot through the root at the bur.

Hard cut at f36 from the hook to a pink-on-pink mucosa field with a thin soft grey needle and no tooth, cheek or jaw landmark; the viewer cannot tell where in the mouth the injection and incision happen (f36-f140). Repair: open the injection on a slightly wider view that includes the second molar crown, then push in, and darken the background for needle contrast. Proof: f40 shows a molar landmark and a crisp needle.

Bone over the tooth is a beige speckled slab with knife-straight edges and a pointed lower end, like cork or sponge laid on the tooth, not continuous jaw with a cortex (f180-f300). Repair: blend the cover into surrounding alveolar bone with a rounded cortical lip and a denser outer layer. Proof: f210 shows bone continuous with the socket rim.

The groove reads as a flat olive-brown speckled disc or coin on the tooth neck (f372-f395, f777-f800) instead of a cut slot, so 'split along the groove' has no groove to follow. Repair: cut a slot across the neck with pale dentin walls and depth shading. Proof: f780 and f375 show a slot, no disc.

Extracted root pieces do not read as roots: one is a flat beige fan with radial ridges like a shell or cracker, the other a red-marbled wedge (also f567-f600 in the socket). Repair: model two tapered root halves with cementum colour and a small canal on the cut face. Proof: f768 shows tapered root halves beside the crown.

Root surface reads as glossy red-and-cream marbled meat or glazed candy, and its broken edge is fringed with torn-paper slivers (f307-f557, f0-f35). Repair: matte yellowish cementum with thin blood film and a clean fractured dentin edge. Proof: f501 and f367.

Thin wire loops and arcs around the bur tip read as bent paper-clip wires attached to the handpiece (f186-f371), with hard-edged pink splat shapes beside them. Repair: remove the loops, show rotation through a blurred bur and fine spray. Proof: f234 and f330 show a bare bur with mist.

Reflected flap rim reads as a glossy red hose with pinched segment joints circling the socket, and the incision margin as a regular red beaded chain (f150-f600). Repair: thin tapered flap edge with a pale underside and irregular wet bleeding. Proof: f434 and f167.

Socket bed is an oversized trough with a regular scalloped brown rim like pie crust; the root lies exposed along its full length instead of seated in bone (f372-f485). Repair: tighten the socket around the root and give the rim a smooth cortical edge with cancellous texture inside. Proof: f390 and f434.

Scalpel blade reads as thick white marbled plastic, and the blood on its tip (and on the elevator tip at f33) is a hard-edged jagged red cut-out. Repair: brushed steel with a bevel highlight, slimmer blade profile, soft wet blood. Proof: f100.

Suction beat is 17 frames (0.57 s), too short to read the caption, and shows a whitish wedge-shaped streak with no pool of blood being removed. Repair: hold at least 30 frames and show a blood pool draining at the tip. Proof: f300 shows the pool level and the tip.

First root exits by swinging past the lens as a motion-blurred smear covering the left third of the frame for about f532-f548, so the delivered piece is soft at its key moment. Repair: lift the root up and out while it stays in focus for at least 8 frames. Proof: f540 shows a sharp root clear of the socket.
Suture thread is drawn as a sawtooth zigzag polyline rather than a smooth curve (f690-f709). Repair: smooth spline thread with slack and tension. Proof: f701.

Thin pale hoop line circles the root at the crown junction before any cut, and at f0 its lower arc hangs free below the tooth like a wire loop (f0-f35, f307-f415, f777-f800). Repair: remove the curve or turn it into a subtle surface colour change at the neck. Proof: f0 and f367 show no line.

Second caption line overlaps the top of the crown specimen on the tray (f728-f776). Repair: lower the specimen framing or raise the caption block. Proof: f768 shows clear space between caption and crown.

Socket blood changes from dark red to pale pink in roughly eight frames (about f626-f640), reading as a material swap more than a flush. Repair: spread the dilution over 20+ frames with visible flow from the syringe tip. Proof: f630 shows a mid-dilution swirl.

From the cue sheet: the suction recording starts at f290 and runs 1.23 s, about 20 frames into the sectioning shot where no suction tip is visible; the drill recording ends near f252 while the bur stays engaged until f289. Repair: trim suction to the cut at f307 and extend the drill bed to f289. Proof: cue sheet shows suction ending by f307 and drill covering f186-f289.
Step chip text ('02 / 07 | 절개') and the single '치관' tag are small at phone size. Repair: enlarge chip and tag text by about a third. Proof: f100 and f33.

anatomy.evidence: Crown with cusps and fissures reads well (f434, f768) and the step order is coherent, but the second molar is a free fang with no septum (f567), the root lies in an oversized trough (f367), the bone is a slab (f234) and the root pieces are shards (f768).

materials.evidence: Wet textured mucosa and enamel are credible (f100, f167, f300); scalpel reads as white plastic (f100), root as marbled glaze (f501), bone as cork (f234), flap rim as red hose (f434).

lighting.evidence: Soft studio light with wet speculars and shallow depth of field holds across shots with no clipping (f300 crown, f634 fluid highlights); palette is uniformly red-pink so the needle shot lacks separation (f60).

camera_motion.evidence: Incision opening behind the blade (f81-f140), flap lift (f141-f185), crown split (f390-f415) and crown lift (f416-f459) show cause and effect; drill is static with a parked bur (f186-f264), the root exits as a blur (f540) and the suture knot pops in (f713).

composition.evidence: Captions are large and clear and the subject sits in the upper-middle band (f33, f367), but the lower 40% is blurred pink in most shots, there is no establishing context (f60), and the caption overlaps the crown on the tray (f768).

hook.evidence: The tooth cracks with blood inside the first second under a clear caption (f0-f35) and the loop returns to the same shot (f777-f800); the subject is partly ambiguous (olive disc, marbled root) and the cut at f36 lands on the weakest image.
